cohort: This study included 1,602,638 singleton neonates delivered between 24 and 42 weeks of gestation, of which 44,359 were classified as LGA.
finding: Being large-for-gestational-age (LGA) is associated with increased risks of perinatal complications in term and late preterm neonates, but these risks are not increased, and in some cases even decreased, in moderate, very, and extremely preterm groups.
mod_finding: LGA neonates in term and late preterm groups exhibited higher risks of primary cesarean section, while LGA was associated with lower risks of primary cesarean section in the very preterm group.
gest_age: 24-42 weeks of gestation, categorized into term (37-42 weeks), late preterm (34-36 weeks), moderate preterm (32-33 weeks), very preterm (28-31 weeks), and extremely preterm (24-27 weeks).
